subject: Feasibility check: Acme on-prem / VPC deployment — architecture & resourcing
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>, Acme Security <acme_security@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Feasibility check: Acme on-prem / VPC deployment — architecture & resourcing

Hi all,

Acme (see attached requirements) has asked for a Private deployment option. Their asks are two tracks:

- VPC-private control plane (managed by Redwood in their VPC) with customer KMS/HSM integration
- Full on-prem air-gapped option (single-tenant cluster in their DC) for the most sensitive workloads

They've listed desired timeline of ~3 months from contract signature and require SOC-2 evidence, audit logs retention (90d), and a hardware spec that looks like 3x A100-class GPUs per cluster.

Questions I need from product/infra/security to prepare an internal feasibility note for legal/procurement:
1) Architecture: major gaps vs our current Private offering (networking, packaging, control plane separation).
2) Resourcing: rough FTE estimate (eng + infra + docs + QA + support) and an expected time-to-delivery range.
3) Compliance: what evidence we can provide quickly vs what requires work (e.g., HSM integration, audit logging tweaks).
4) Commercial implications: should sales expect an engineering carve-out, and any recommended guardrails for SLA/credits?

Attached: acme_requirements.pdf (customer list).

Connor
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Feasibility check: Acme on-prem / VPC deployment — architecture & resourcing

Thanks for the context, Connor. Quick technical read:

- Control plane: our current Private control plane expects outbound connectivity for telemetry and license checks. For VPC-managed control plane we can isolate traffic to customer-managed endpoints; for air-gapped on-prem we need an alternate bootstrap flow (offline license/key exchange).
- Networking: Acme will need a stable internal DNS + L4 load balancer and routable subnets for GPU nodes. We'll need to confirm their L2/L3 constraints (no multicast).
- Hardware: A100-class is fine but we should validate NVLink topology expectations. We can support mixed node types but recommend uniform GPU types per cluster.
- HSM/KMS: We have an integration adapter for popular KMS vendors but HSM support (PKCS#11) will require a small native shim (~2-3 sprint tasks).
- Packaging: for on-prem air-gapped we must produce an OCI bundle + offline installer and documented steps for firmware/driver install.

Rough resourcing (ballpark):
- Tech lead (eng): 0.6 FTE for 4 months
- Infra/packaging: 0.4 FTE for 3 months (to build offline installer + automation)
- QA/bench: 0.3 FTE for 2 months
- Docs + runbook: 0.2 FTE for 1 month
- Support onboarding (CS): 0.2 FTE during rollout

Risk: audit logging and retention change will touch existing trace pipeline; ETA for that work depends on whether we can reuse current retention policy flags or need a separate storage tier.

I've attached an internal checklist I usually send for on-prem engagements (onprem-deploy-checklist.xlsx). Happy to sketch a simple architecture diagram if folks want.

—Dev
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Feasibility check: Acme on-prem / VPC deployment — architecture & resourcing

Thanks Dev — this is a useful start. A few product notes:

- Feature parity: we need to confirm API parity for telemetry and user-facing endpoints (particularly streaming/long-poll behaviors) before we commit to parity claims in the SOW.
- Rollouts & fallbacks: Product will need a canary/fallback plan so we can failover to hosted model variants if on-prem performance/regressions occur. That's additional product work (approx 1-2 sprints).
- Storying: can we convert Dev's FTE numbers into story points for roadmap planning? I want a high/med/low estimate so we can surface to PM leadership.

Commercially, we should flag that on-prem will be a premium add-on (engineering pass-through + support SLA). Evelyn — can you confirm the customer's procurement timeline and whether they expect an enterprise discount or credits for SLAs?

I'll kick off an RFC draft in the linked Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Aq-example-RFC) — please comment directly.

Laura Bennett
Product Lead, Private Deployments

Quick commercial note — Acme's procurement pinged me this morning. They want pricing guidance this week and would like to know if we can offer any of the following:

- 10% discount if they commit to a 12-month Dedicated + on-prem pilot
- Credits for SLA breaches during the initial 90 days

Connor — do you want me to float the discount or hold until we have a formal estimate from Eng/Product? If the technical ask looks heavy we may need an executive exception for both timeline and credit.

Summary and next steps (per thread):

- Action: schedule a 60-min technical sync with Acme (Dev, Marcus, Connor) — I'll propose Monday 10am PT.
- Tech lead: Dev will be the internal technical owner; estimate we should budget 0.6 FTE eng + 0.4 FTE infra/packaging + QA/docs as listed.
- Timeline: realistic plan is 3–4 months for a minimal VPC-managed Private option with HSM adapter; pure air-gapped on-prem will add ~3 weeks for offline installation validation and driver/version testing.
- Compliance: we can provide SOC-2 artifact summaries; HSM PKCS#11 will be an add-on. Marcus — can you confirm required logging retention tiering?
- Commercial: Evelyn, please hold off on firm discounting until we have a scoped SOW. We can offer a pilot pricing structure but credit exceptions need leader sign-off.

I'll create the RFC and initial scope doc in Drive and share the HubSpot deal (HubSpot:ACME-0045). Attachments: initial-scope-estimate.csv.
